correctness.rationale: Exact stochastic integral multiplier on each sampling cell follows from stable characteristic functions and variation of constants. Positive alpha-stable subordinator variable V times independent standard Cauchy C has characteristic exp(-|u|^alpha), yielding via Poisson log potential E log|e^(theta tau)+dVC|=0.5 E log(e^(2theta tau)+d^2 V^2). Log absolute moment integrable by stable tails/local density and log-moment bounds; sampled log SLLN applies. Within-cell sup has finite log+ expectation using p<alpha maximal moment and deterministic-kernel integration by parts; Borel-Cantelli removes k^-1 fluctuation, with sampled times giving reverse limsup bound. Nonzero gain strictly increases exponent; continuity and divergence yield unique critical gain theta<0. Cauchy endpoint bcrit=|theta|/sigma sqrt(coth(-theta*tau/2)). Independent numerical Cauchy drift/gain/critical cases checked; source verify.py read, not rerun. Finite checks are not the a.s. proof.
residual_risks: No full continuous-time t^-1 log|X_t| limit is asserted: within-cell zeros/near-zeros can make liminf different.
Only centered symmetric stable noise and sampled multiplicative noise coefficient; no skew, state-feedback drift or Brownian case.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge finding concerns exact almost-sure logarithmic sample-product exponent for symmetric alpha-stable innovations with 0<alpha<=1 and feedback multiplying the sampled state in the NOISE coefficient. The Brownian same-architecture stabilization theorem has alpha=2 and cannot extend its finite-variance sufficient condition to these infinite-first-moment laws; Zhang 2026 uses alpha>1 and sufficient results; G-Levy results concern nonlinear expectation/moment notions. The stable/Cauchy mixture and Poisson identity are classical and are not claimed original. New result is exact all-gain pathwise exponent and obstruction in this parameter regime. Relevant full G-Levy paper unavailable, so historical priority explicitly qualified.
residual_risks: Full G-Levy discrete-feedback primary text inaccessible; it might contain a relevant unexamined specialization.
Classical stochastic-control and Cauchy-log-potential literature could include an equivalent previously unnoticed scalar sampling application.

value.rationale: Sharp stability/instability boundary for an established sampled stochastic-control architecture precisely at the infinite-mean heavy-tail range 0<alpha<=1. It overturns naive extension of Brownian noise stabilizability by showing the universal nonnegative increase in upper a.s. exponent and gives explicit Cauchy gain threshold; control researchers can use the exact rate rather than insufficient moment criteria.
residual_risks: Importance depends on the deliberately limited symmetric scalar sampled-noise family; no general nonlinear or multidimensional claim.
